commitResults.messageTitle: Hold TAssist data in ModelManager
commitResults.messageBody:
Group, student, GUI and weekly-record features all need to reach the
TAssist data through the Model, but the Model only holds the
AddressBook.

Let's make ModelManager hold a copy of a TAssist beside the
AddressBook. Keep the AddressBook so existing commands keep working
until it is removed.

TAssist data is not saved yet, so the app starts with no groups.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let the Model manage tutorial groups
commitResults.messageBody:
Group commands need to add groups, look them up and switch the active
group, but the Model cannot do any of that yet.

Let's delegate these group operations from the Model to TAssist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let the Model add and remove students in a group
commitResults.messageBody:
Student commands need to add students to a group and remove them, but
the Model cannot do that yet.

Let's delegate these student operations from the Model to TAssist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep observable views of the active group
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI must show the active group and its students, and update them
as soon as either changes, but the Model offers no way to observe
them.

Let's expose the active group as a property, and the active group's
students as a list that follows whichever group is active.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expose the active group and its students to the UI
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI talks to Logic, not to the Model, so it cannot reach the new
active group views yet.

Let's add them to Logic so the GUI can show the active group and its
students.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe how the Model holds TAssist data in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide says the TAssist classes are not used by the app,
which is no longer true.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain how the UI observes the active group in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
Developers building the group, student and GUI features need to know
how the active group views stay up to date, and why they are built
this way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the active group's name in the header
commitResults.messageBody:
The header always says the active group is "None", even though the
Model now knows which group is active.

Let's show the active group's name there, and update it whenever
another group becomes active. Long names are shortened, with the full
name in a tooltip.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a panel that lists the active group's students
commitResults.messageBody:
The Students screen should list the students of the active group, but
the only roster panel lists AddressBook contacts.

Let's add a panel that lists the active group's students by name and
student ID. When there is nothing to list, it says whether no group is
active or the active group has no students yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the active group's students on the Students screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Students screen still lists AddressBook contacts, which TAssist
users do not manage.

Let's show the new student panel there instead, and remove the
contact roster. Contact commands keep working until AddressBook is
removed, but contacts are no longer shown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the Students screen in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide says the Students screen lists contacts, which no longer
matches the app.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the student roster UI in the DG
commitResults.messageBody: The DG still describes the contact roster and its manual tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use one phrase when no group is active
commitResults.messageBody:
The header said "None", the Students screen said "No active group",
and the previews pointed to Students in their own words, so the same
state read differently in each place.

Let's say "No active group" everywhere, hide the "Active group"
caption when it would read twice, and drop the group caption on the
Students screen, as the header already names the group. Let's also
remove the extra line from the previews.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the tutorial groups in the group strip
commitResults.messageBody:
The strip below the header said "Tutorial groups coming soon", even
though the app now holds groups and knows which one is active.

Let's show a chip for each group there, as in the UI mock-up, and
highlight the active one. When there are no groups, the strip says so.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the current screen after contact commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Contact commands switch to the Students screen, which no longer shows
contacts, so the user sees nothing happen.

Let's keep the current screen after any command that does not ask for
a screen. Contact commands still report their result in the feedback
box until AddressBook is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show help only on the Help screen
commitResults.messageBody:
help printed the command reference into the small feedback box, while
F1, the menu and view help showed the same reference on the Help
screen. The feedback box fits only a few lines, so the reference there
was hard to read.

Let's make help open the Help screen and only confirm in the feedback
box. help TOPIC opens the Help screen at that topic's commands. The
help text formatter is no longer used, so let's remove it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit the feedback box to its message
commitResults.messageBody:
The feedback box was fixed at 62 to 90 pixels, so a message with a
command's usage showed two lines and a scroll bar. Feedback is how
users learn whether a command worked, so it should be readable at a
glance.

Let's grow the box with its message, from one line up to six. Only
longer messages scroll, and short ones leave more room for the screen
above.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the reworked workspace in the UG and DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides still describe help in the feedback box, a fixed feedback
box, contact commands opening Students, and no group strip.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md for AI agents
commitResults.messageBody:
AI coding agents used by team members do not know the course
constraints, the Java and Git conventions, or the PR workflow, so
their output can violate graded requirements.

Let's add AGENTS.md describing those rules, and a CLAUDE.md that
imports it. Stop ignoring both files so that they are shared with
the whole team.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add StudentBuilder test utility
commitResults.messageBody:
Feature tests need students with sensible defaults instead of
each test constructing names and IDs by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add GroupBuilder test utility
commitResults.messageBody:
Build a group with a default name and any number of students. Each
build() returns a new Group, so tests never share a mutable group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add TypicalStudents test fixtures
commitResults.messageBody:
Share one set of students across tests. Two extra students are
kept outside the typical list for tests that add a new student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add TypicalGroups test fixtures
commitResults.messageBody:
Provide typical groups T01, T02 and T03, which have three, two and
no students. Group is mutable, so each getter returns a new group
to stop tests from affecting one another.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add TAssistBuilder test utility
commitResults.messageBody:
Build a TAssist from groups and an optional active group. The active
group is set when build() is called, so it may be named before its
group is added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add typical TAssist data to TypicalGroups
commitResults.messageBody:
Provide a full database of the typical groups, so feature tests
can start from the same data. No group is active, and tests can
use TAssistBuilder to choose one.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for typical group fixtures
commitResults.messageBody:
Check the typical groups and TAssist hold the expected students, and
that each call returns new objects, since fixtures must not be shared
between tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for TAssistBuilder
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover naming the active group before its group is added, a missing
active group, and copying an existing TAssist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use typical students in StudentTest

commitResults.messageTitle: Use typical students in UniqueStudentListTest

Drop the students that the test built by hand, and build the
same-ID student with StudentBuilder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use typical fixtures in GroupTest
commitResults.messageBody: Drop the group name and students that the test built by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use typical groups in UniqueGroupListTest
commitResults.messageBody:
Create a new typical group for each test, so that a test cannot
change a group that another test uses.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use typical fixtures in TAssistTest
commitResults.messageBody:
Start from the typical TAssist instead of adding groups and students
by hand in every test, and use TAssistBuilder to set the active group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document shared TAssist test fixtures
commitResults.messageBody:
Tell developers which builders and typical data exist, and why the
mutable ones must be created fresh in every test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add value semantics and tests for HelpEntry

Add equals, hashCode and toString, cover the constructor validation with

Add HelpCatalog.TOPICS, isValidTopic, filterByTopic and getTopicHeading so

commitResults.messageTitle: Document when the active group property notifies

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JSON adapter for students
commitResults.messageBody:
The TAssist data file needs to hold each student's name and ID, and a
wrong manual edit to either must be reported rather than crash the app.

Let's add a Jackson-friendly student that checks both fields when it is
turned back into a Student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JSON adapter for tutorial groups
commitResults.messageBody:
Each tutorial group in the data file holds its name and its students.
A manual edit may leave out the student list, add an empty entry, or
repeat a student ID within the group.

Let's add a Jackson-friendly group that reads a missing student list as
no students, and rejects empty entries and repeated student IDs with a
message naming the group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JSON form of the whole TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
The data file holds every tutorial group and which group is active. A
manual edit may repeat a group name in a different case, name an active
group that does not exist, or leave out either field.

Let's add a serializable TAssist that reads a missing group list as no
groups and a missing active group as none, and rejects repeated group
names and an unknown active group with a specific message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JSON file storage for TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
TAssist data lives only in memory, so tutorial groups and students are
lost when the app closes.

Let's add a storage class that saves TAssist data to a JSON file and
reads it back, reporting a missing file as no data and an unreadable or
invalid file as a loading error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let Storage read and save TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
The JSON storage for TAssist data is not reachable through the Storage
component, so Logic and the app launcher cannot use it.

Let's give Storage methods to read and save TAssist data, and keep the
TAssist data file at data/tassist.json.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save TAssist data after each command
commitResults.messageBody:
Successful commands save AddressBook data, so changes to tutorial
groups, students and the active group are lost when the app closes.

Let's save TAssist data instead, so the data file follows every
successful command other than view. A failed save is still reported to
the user.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load TAssist data from the data file at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Every run starts with no tutorial groups, and a first launch fills the
app with sample contacts.

Let's restore groups, students and the active group from the TAssist
data file when the app starts. A missing file starts an empty TAssist
with no sample data, and an unreadable or invalid file starts an empty
TAssist and logs why the file could not be read. AddressBook data is no
longer loaded.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop wiring AddressBook storage into Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The app no longer reads or saves AddressBook data, so the AddressBook
methods of Storage are unused.

Let's remove them from Storage and StorageManager. The AddressBook
storage classes stay until the AddressBook code is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe TAssist data on the Storage screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage screen says contact commands are saved and a first launch
shows sample contacts, which is no longer true.

Let's say that tutorial groups and students are saved and that a first
launch starts empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the TAssist data file in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG says contact data is saved to data/addressbook.json and that a
first launch shows sample data, which is no longer true.

Let's describe what TAssist saves, where the data file is, what it
looks like, and what happens when it is missing or invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show TAssist storage in the storage class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage class diagram shows AddressBook storage, which Storage no
longer uses.

Let's show the TAssist storage classes in its place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe saving and loading TAssist data in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says TAssist data is not saved and describes AddressBook
storage, and its manual tests expect sample contacts on first launch.

Let's describe the TAssist data file, how it is saved and loaded, how
later features add their own records to it, and how to test a missing
or invalid file by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test loading TAssist data at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading the data file at startup has no tests, so a regression in how
a missing, valid or invalid file is handled would go unnoticed.

Let's make the model setup in MainApp visible to tests in its package,
and test each of the three cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a data file that holds only null
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file whose whole content is null makes JsonUtil return
Optional.of(null), which throws NullPointerException and crashes the
app at startup instead of starting with an empty TAssist.

Let's treat such a file as unreadable, so it is reported like any other
invalid file. This also covers the preferences file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Quote the active group name in load errors
commitResults.messageBody:
When the active group in the data file is blank, the error reads "The
active group  is not in the group list.", which hides what is wrong.

Let's quote the name, so a blank or space-padded name is visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy TAssist storage Javadoc and message names
commitResults.messageBody:
One saveTAssist overload documents only one of its two parameters, and
the group adapter names its missing-field message differently from the
student adapter.

Let's document both parameters and use the student adapter's naming
for the group's missing-field message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check why rejected TAssist files are rejected
commitResults.messageBody:
Some storage tests only check that an invalid file is rejected, so they
would still pass if it were rejected for the wrong reason.

Let's also check the reason, and name the active group test after both
things it covers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention the active group on the Storage screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage screen lists tutorial groups and students as saved data,
but the active group is saved too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify failed commands and contacts in the docs
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG says a failed command does not change data, but a command whose
save fails has already changed the data in memory. The DG paragraph on
contact commands does not say that contacts are no longer saved.

Let's restore the UG's earlier wording about failed commands, and say
in the DG that contacts are not saved.

commitResults.messageTitle: Title the student card with the group name
commitResults.messageBody:
The card said "Student roster" and showed the count at the far right,
repeating the Students tab and the active group shown elsewhere. Title
it with the group name and a count badge instead.

Show the empty state in place of the table, so that column headings
no longer sit above an explanation, and center its text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge the header and group strip into one top bar
commitResults.messageBody:
The dark header and the group strip took two rows, and the active group
appeared in the header, the strip and the student card. Replace them
with one light bar that holds the brand, the group chips and a Help
button.

The menu bar is removed. Help stays on F1, the Help button and the help
command, and the window can still be closed or exited with exit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Open screens from a navigation bar
commitResults.messageBody:
The tab strip gave all seven screens equal weight, including four that
are still previews, and Help and Storage looked like data screens.

Hide the tab strip and open the screens from a bar in the top chrome:
the screens that hold group data come first, and Groups, Help and
Storage sit at the right. A dot marks a screen that is still a preview.
Each tooltip names the equivalent view command, and clicking keeps the
keyboard focus in the command box.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark command feedback with a state icon
commitResults.messageBody:
The feedback was a mint box that only turned pink on failure. Show a
check or a cross beside the message on a white row, and tint the row
only for failures.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show shortcuts in the footer and tidy the student table
commitResults.messageBody:
The "Enter" hint in the command box told the user nothing new. Put the
F1 and Esc shortcuts in the footer instead, and show the command box
border at full strength only while it has focus.

Give the student table fixed column widths, so that a student ID sits
beside the name on wide windows, and let the row dividers span the
whole table.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the reworked top bar and feedback in the docs
commitResults.messageBody:
Update the User Guide, the Developer Guide and the UI class diagram for
the navigation bar, the group chips in the top bar, the feedback icon
and the footer shortcuts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the footer status dot visible in narrow windows
commitResults.messageBody:
The dot shrank to an ellipsis at the minimum window width. Also render
that width in the UI smoke test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark a failed command in the footer
commitResults.messageBody:
The footer said "Command failed" beside the same green dot as a
success. Turn the dot red for a failed command, so that the two cases
differ at a glance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Center the feedback row and enlarge the failure icon
commitResults.messageBody:
A one-line message sat a few pixels above the middle of its row, and
the cross in a failure looked smaller than the check mark. Drop the
text area's own padding, rebalance the row padding, and enlarge the
cross.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that the GUI is adapted from the mockup
commitResults.messageBody:
The Acknowledgements and the style sheet said that the GUI follows the
team-supplied mockup. The top bar and the navigation bar now differ from
it, so say that the design is based on the mockup and name what is
different.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the real UI on the home page and README
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui.png was the team's mock-up, which shows features that do not exist
yet and the old dark header. Replace it with a screenshot of the
implemented GUI.

Keep the mock-up as UiMockup.png and link it from the Developer Guide,
so that it stays in the repository as the design reference.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the User Guide screenshot
commitResults.messageBody:
The screenshot showed the contact roster and the old header. Show the
GUI as it appears on the first launch, as the Quick Start describes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the help and navigation descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide still said that HelpCommand formats the entries with
HelpCatalog.format, which no longer exists, and that a navigation button
does everything view SCREEN does, although it does not show the feedback
message. Describe what the code does.

Also rename the stale v1.2 testing heading and drop the unused
card-caption style.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #83 from linziyang2025-byte/52-show-active-group
commitResults.messageBody: Show the active group and its students in the GUI
